Consultation quick card

Read this page first • 5-minute plan

Over the next three to five years, Square Enix should establish a human-centered AI development policy: progressively integrate validated AI assistance into programming, testing, debugging and internal tools, retain human creative control, and protect human authorship of final franchise-defining content.

Timing: Slides 1–6 ≈ 4:00. Slide 7 ≈ 1:00 for the whole-group conclusion. Seven Q&A backup slides and four reference slides are hidden in the normal slideshow.

The three rules to remember

Boundary: protect designated final core expression.

Evidence: expand only after verified net value and quality.

Accountability: named humans own decisions throughout.

Read before the consultation

Q02: already using AI?
Q03: why long term?
Q06: do players hate AI art?
Q15: incompatible productivity numbers?
Q21: costs and savings?
Q32: what would change your mind?

A response pattern, not a list of rebuttals

Answer the question → use the relevant evidence → acknowledge its limit → explain the policy consequence. Where the teacher identifies a valid limit, concede it. A quotation supports a premise; it does not turn a proposed policy into a proven fact.

Unresolved team input: the other three final recommendations are not confirmed. Slide 7 has explicit placeholders. Replace them before presenting; do not infer them from preliminary analysis topics.

This pack prepares for 32 plausible questions, not every possible question. Main slides use brief claims and visuals; the notes supply reasoning and transitions. Use your own delivery and retain your source trail.

Evidence: what the source measured or stated. Inference: our interpretation connecting it to this client. Proposal: the decision, scope and timetable we recommend.

Two compatible openings

Reasoning First

Present the opportunity and the decision problem, then develop the recommendation.

  • Technical uses already exist in game development.
  • Square Enix already announced a QA automation target.
  • Two questions: where is AI appropriate, and when is expansion justified?

Bridge: But the value of AI depends on what we ask it to do.

Recommendation First

Replace only Slide 1; retain Slides 2–7 and the same timing.

  • State the 3–5-year human-centered policy immediately.
  • Name the two boundaries: validated technical assistance and protected core authorship.
  • Preview the support: use-specific reception, measured value, accountable scaling.

Bridge: The first reason for setting boundaries is that player acceptance depends on the use.

Switch rule: replace only Slide 1. Both files retain the same Slides 2–7 and the same approximate total. Do not show two openings. The evidence-first deck develops the recommendation; the alternative announces the destination before supporting it.

Assessment alignment

The supplied CAES9821 guide requires 5–6 minutes per person (p. 27), permits recommendations supported by relevant literature (p. 8), and assesses research and feedback reflection in the consultation (p. 25). This pack uses outlines and cue prompts rather than a complete presentation script.

Slide 1 | AI has technical potential—where should it be used?

0:00–0:40 • 40 seconds

Claim. Technical AI is worth evaluating, but Square Enix needs both benefits and boundaries.

Evidence. Unity (2026), chart 2.1: 62% coding assistance, 35% automated playtesting, 28% code QA. Square Enix announced a 70% QA/debugging automation target in November 2025 (2025b, p. 5).

Reasoning. Reported industry use identifies feasible candidates; the existing company target makes this a question about responsible expansion, not first adoption.

What to cover

  • 0–8 s: Link from the previous speaker without repeating their findings. Introduce the question of improving development while preserving franchise identity.
  • 8–23 s: Point to coding, playtesting and QA. Explain that the bars measure reported use, not productivity.
  • 23–32 s: Acknowledge Square Enix already announced QA automation. Say the proposal builds on existing activity.
  • 32–40 s: Frame two questions: where AI fits, and when its use should expand.

Transition. But the value of AI depends on what we ask it to do.

Limit to retain. The 70% is an announced target, not an achieved result. Unity is a multi-response survey of 300 developers, fielded in 2025.

Sources: Unity (2026) [S01]; Square Enix Holdings Co., Ltd. (2025b) [S03]

Slide 2 | Player acceptance depends on the use

0:40–1:25 • 45 seconds

Claim. Different applications need different boundaries.

Evidence. Game8 survey: approximately 84% positive for debugging/balance support, 75% for models/terrain, 48% for stories and 45% for voices (Dapa, 2025). Company creative priorities: Square Enix Holdings Co., Ltd. (2025a, p. 7).

Reasoning. Differences within one survey reject a simple all-AI rule. Combined with the importance of creative identity, they motivate cautious treatment of core content.

What to cover

  • 0–10 s: Identify the survey: 205 Game8 users, online, July 2025.
  • 10–25 s: Contrast development support with story and voice generation. Acknowledge the high model/terrain acceptance.
  • 25–35 s: Explain that creative replacement and technical support should not automatically receive the same policy.
  • 35–45 s: Concede the sample is not representative; connect the distinction to Square Enix’s creative priorities.

Transition. That suggests selective integration, rather than a blanket yes or no.

Limit to retain. Not a representative Square Enix fan sample. Below 50% positive does not mean a majority opposed. The survey alone does not establish an artwork ban.

Sources: Dapa (2025) [S07]; Square Enix Holdings Co., Ltd. (2025a) [S02]

Slide 3 | Adopt selectively; protect core creation

1:25–1:50 • 25 seconds

Claim. Keep human control over all creative decisions, with a stronger human-authorship rule for designated final core content.

Evidence. The boundary is a proposed policy informed by the company’s stated creative priorities, differentiated reception and authorship research (Square Enix Holdings Co., Ltd., 2025a; Dapa, 2025; Bellaiche et al., 2023).

Reasoning. Evidence supports differentiation; management must still choose and document the boundary. Non-core does not automatically mean safe.

What to cover

  • 0–8 s: State the intermediate recommendation: prioritise verifiable technical assistance.
  • 8–17 s: Name the protected examples—final signature character designs, key artwork and main-story content.
  • 17–25 s: Distinguish human authorship from merely approving AI output. Other/mixed uses need separate assessment.

Transition. However, being eligible for a pilot does not mean a workflow has proved its value.

Limit to retain. This is a consultancy policy proposal, not an empirical finding or existing Square Enix rule. No permanent ban on all generative visuals is claimed.

Sources: Square Enix Holdings Co., Ltd. (2025a) [S02]; Dapa (2025) [S07]; Bellaiche et al. (2023) [S08]; DORA (2026) [S11]

Slide 4 | Verify gains before expanding

1:50–2:30 • 40 seconds

Claim. Expansion needs demonstrated net value, maintained quality and human sign-off.

Evidence. Cui et al. (2026): +26.08% completed tasks, SE 10.3 percentage points, pooled 4,867 developers. METR early-2025: +19% task time in a narrow setting (Becker et al., 2025); its 2026 update cautions that newer estimates are unreliable.

Reasoning. These are different outcomes and contexts, not a pooled score. Potential benefits warrant local measurement, including review and rework.

What to cover

  • 0–10 s: Acknowledge credible positive evidence, without promising the same effect for Square Enix.
  • 10–20 s: Note contrasting historical evidence and the 2026 update. Do not subtract or average the figures.
  • 20–30 s: Explain the full workflow: generate, check, fix and integrate. A faster draft may not save total effort.
  • 30–40 s: Define the decision gate: verified net value, quality maintained, responsible human approval.

Transition. To apply these conditions consistently, they need to become a shared working policy.

Limit to retain. Neither study estimates Square Enix savings. Human review is necessary but does not guarantee correctness. No universal minimum gain is asserted.

Sources: Cui et al. (2026) [S04]; Becker et al. (2025) [S05]; Becker et al. (2026) [S06]; Tabassi (2023) [S09]; Autio et al. (2024) [S10]

Slide 5 | Make human-centered AI a working policy

2:30–3:20 • 50 seconds

Claim. The policy makes the preceding choices enforceable across teams.

Evidence. DORA (2026) recommends cross-functional ownership, clear permissions and a living policy. Tabassi (2023, MAP 3.5; MANAGE 4) supports oversight and monitoring; Autio et al. (2024) supports output and supplier controls.

Reasoning. Classification defines scope; responsible people verify results; conditional expansion and feedback prevent a one-time approval becoming permanent.

What to cover

  • 0–12 s: Show the three-stage flow: classify, verify, scale and review.
  • 12–24 s: Classify: protect final core authorship; approve the tool, data and use case for eligible technical work. Hold unresolved uses.
  • 24–36 s: Verify: engineering/QA own measurable checks; creative leads own the creative boundary; legal/security approve relevant data and rights.
  • 36–50 s: Scale only after the gate is met, with a rollback route. Pre-approve standard workflows so every small task does not need committee review.

Transition. A shared rule is the starting point; sustained use also needs training, integration and repeated evaluation.

Limit to retain. Roles are proposed, not a description of current internal practice. The flow is our synthesis, not an official NIST diagram. This does not assert Square Enix lacks policies.

Sources: Tabassi (2023) [S09]; Autio et al. (2024) [S10]; DORA (2026) [S11]

Slide 6 | Build capability over three to five years

3:20–4:00 • 40 seconds

Claim. The long-term deliverable is a repeatable organizational capability—not a six-month experiment or a policy PDF.

Evidence. Square Enix describes AI-related training and cross-project knowledge sharing (2025a, p. 20). DORA (2025) emphasizes organizational systems; Tabassi (2023) provides continuing monitoring and improvement principles.

Reasoning. One successful pilot cannot establish cross-studio repeatability. Staff capabilities, shared evaluation and integration need ongoing investment and review.

What to cover

  • 0–10 s: State the full long-term recommendation, combining selective technical adoption and protected human creative control.
  • 10–25 s: Walk the roadmap: Year 1 establish and pilot; Years 2–3 integrate validated workflows; Years 4–5 optimise or retire them.
  • 25–33 s: Explain that pilots begin now; the time horizon is proposed, not research-derived. Expansion stays conditional.
  • 33–40 s: Close your part with the decision: authorise a staged capability program, not a fixed AI-use quota.

Transition. This development capability supports the wider strategy our group has proposed.

Limit to retain. No budget, guaranteed savings or return is inferred from public data. Training and integration use existing functions where feasible.

Sources: Square Enix Holdings Co., Ltd. (2025a) [S02]; Tabassi (2023) [S09]; DORA (2026) [S11]; DORA (2025) [S12]

Slide 7 | A coherent plan for Square Enix

4:00–5:00 • 60 seconds

Claim. Synthesize all four confirmed recommendations around the client’s production and distribution objectives.

Evidence. The other three final recommendations have not been supplied. This slide deliberately contains editable placeholders, not invented group claims.

Reasoning. The conclusion should connect decisions and implementation, not introduce new evidence or repeat the full AI argument.

What to cover

  • 0–10 s: Re-state the group’s agreed business problem in one sentence.
  • 10–35 s: Summarise each teammate’s confirmed recommendation, its benefit and time horizon. Replace all three placeholders first.
  • 35–48 s: Add your contribution: long-term development capability through selective AI integration and protected creative control.
  • 48–60 s: Explain how the four actions fit together, then finish with the group’s agreed decision request. Add no new findings.

Transition. End the presentation; move to Q&A.

Limit to retain. This is the only content block intentionally left for team input. Do not present placeholders in the assessed version.

Sources: Team inputs; no new evidence.

Q&A rehearsal cards | 1–3

32 question cards

Q01 • Core defense

What exactly are you recommending?

Answer route. A three-to-five-year capability program governed by a human-centered policy: validate technical assistance, protect authorship of designated final core content, assign accountable reviewers, and expand only when benefits and quality justify it. The pilot is one early stage; the outcome is a repeatable cross-team process.

Evidence / quote bank: Square Enix Holdings Co., Ltd. (2025a) [S02]; Tabassi (2023) [S09]; DORA (2026) [S11]
Slide to open: Main 5–6.

Concede. The complete policy and horizon are our recommendation, not a published finding.

Possible follow-up. Which outcomes would you report? Total task effort, accepted quality, full costs and staff capability.

Q02 • Core defense

Square Enix already uses AI. What is new?

Answer route. That is acknowledged, not overlooked. The 2025 plan already sets a QA automation target. Our added proposal is an explicit task boundary and evidence-based expansion process across projects. We would first assess existing policies and strengthen gaps, rather than claim to invent the company’s AI program.

Evidence / quote bank: Square Enix Holdings Co., Ltd. (2025b) [S03]; Square Enix Holdings Co., Ltd. (2025a) [S02]; DORA (2026) [S11]
Slide to open: Main 1; B4.

Concede. We cannot see all internal controls; we do not claim none exist.

Possible follow-up. What would you inspect first? Existing approvals, responsibilities, evidence and training.

Q03 • Core defense

Why is this long term if the first step is a pilot?

Answer route. The pilot tests feasibility; it is not the deliverable. The longer program embeds tools, trains staff, shares evaluations across projects, assigns responsibility and rechecks changing tools. These organizational capabilities continue beyond a pilot and individual game, even if useful gains appear earlier.

Evidence / quote bank: Square Enix Holdings Co., Ltd. (2025a) [S02]; Tabassi (2023) [S09]; DORA (2025) [S12]
Slide to open: Main 6; B5.

Concede. Three to five years is a proposed planning horizon, not a scientifically optimal duration.

Possible follow-up. Why not two years? The milestones can accelerate; readiness determines expansion.

Q&A rehearsal cards | 4–6

Q04 • Core defense

Why not adopt AI everywhere?

Answer route. Applications differ in verifiability, creative significance and audience response. The policy therefore separates protected final expression, approved technical workflows, and unresolved uses. That is a more targeted response than assuming that benefits found in one workflow justify use throughout production.

Evidence / quote bank: Dapa (2025) [S07]; Tabassi (2023) [S09]; DORA (2026) [S11]
Slide to open: Main 2–3; B1.

Concede. Some creative applications may be useful; we do not claim a universal anti-AI audience.

Possible follow-up. Could a non-core visual tool be considered? Yes, through separate rights, quality and creative review.

Q05 • Core defense

Why not prohibit AI entirely?

Answer route. Positive field evidence and game-testing deployments justify investigating useful applications. A blanket ban would discard that possibility. Our alternative permits bounded experimentation while retaining oversight, approved inputs and a stopping rule; it does not require use when conventional tools work better.

Evidence / quote bank: Unity (2026) [S01]; Cui et al. (2026) [S04]; Gillberg et al. (2023) [S13]
Slide to open: Main 1, 4.

Concede. External studies do not guarantee a benefit in this client’s environment.

Possible follow-up. What if no benefit is found? Keep the conventional workflow.

Q06 • Creative boundary

Does your evidence prove players hate AI art?

Answer route. No. The Game8 sample is more positive about some uses, including models and terrain. The evidence supports differentiation. Protecting final signature content is our additional strategic judgment, based on Square Enix’s creative priorities and research indicating that perceived authorship can affect evaluation.

Evidence / quote bank: Dapa (2025) [S07]; Square Enix Holdings Co., Ltd. (2025a) [S02]; Bellaiche et al. (2023) [S08]
Slide to open: Main 2; B6.

Concede. A 205-user self-selected survey cannot represent all fans or establish a universal artwork ban.

Possible follow-up. What would strengthen the boundary? Representative fan research and controlled tests of relevant assets.

Q&A rehearsal cards | 7–9

Q07 • Creative boundary

If 75% accept generated models and terrain, why protect artwork?

Answer route. That result is why the proposal is not a ban on all visual generation. Generic terrain and a signature protagonist design are not interchangeable decisions. We designate core expressive assets for human authorship and assess other uses separately. The line is a disclosed policy choice, not a survey category.

Evidence / quote bank: Dapa (2025) [S07]; Square Enix Holdings Co., Ltd. (2025a) [S02]
Slide to open: Main 3; B1.

Concede. The exact boundary needs a documented creative-team decision.

Possible follow-up. What if a terrain feature defines the franchise? Classify by its role, not its file type.

Q08 • Creative boundary

What counts as franchise-defining content?

Answer route. Propose that creative leads identify final assets central to recognition and narrative identity before production: signature character designs, key artwork and main-story expression. Use a documented asset register. Mixed or disputed cases are escalated; calling something a texture or script does not settle its importance.

Evidence / quote bank: Square Enix Holdings Co., Ltd. (2025a) [S02]; Tabassi (2023) [S09]; DORA (2026) [S11]
Slide to open: B1; B4.

Concede. This operational definition is ours and needs client validation.

Possible follow-up. Who decides? Creative leadership with relevant rights and production owners.

Q09 • Creative boundary

Is human creative control the same as human authorship?

Answer route. No. Control means humans set direction, decide and remain accountable. Authorship means humans create the relevant final expression; merely accepting a generated output is not the same. The recommendation uses control as the general principle and authorship as a stricter rule for designated core content.

Evidence / quote bank: Square Enix Holdings Co., Ltd. (2025a) [S02]; Bellaiche et al. (2023) [S08]; U.S. Copyright Office (2025) [S15]
Slide to open: B1.

Concede. Authorship rules in law depend on jurisdiction and facts; this is a proposed production policy.

Possible follow-up. Does this ban all assistance to artists? No; assess whether assistance replaces protected expression.

Q&A rehearsal cards | 10–12

Q10 • Creative boundary

Could artists still use AI for brainstorming or cleanup?

Answer route. Potentially, but this proposal does not silently approve all such uses. Classify the tool, inputs, rights, and effect on final expression. Non-substitutive assistance can be reviewed separately. Protected final core expression must still meet the human-authorship rule, with provenance records rather than a signature alone.

Evidence / quote bank: Tabassi (2023) [S09]; Autio et al. (2024) [S10]; U.S. Copyright Office (2025) [S15]
Slide to open: B1; B4.

Concede. We have no source proving every cleanup or brainstorming workflow is safe.

Possible follow-up. How to prevent generated drafts leaking into finals? Asset records and checks at production handoffs.

Q11 • Creative boundary

What if attitudes change or AI art becomes indistinguishable?

Answer route. Quality and detectability are not the only considerations; authorship, rights and creative strategy also matter. Reassess the boundary on relevant audience and rights evidence through creative governance. A technical pilot does not automatically authorize a change to final creative production.

Evidence / quote bank: Bellaiche et al. (2023) [S08]; Tabassi (2023) [S09]; Dapa (2025) [S07]
Slide to open: B6.

Concede. We do not predict permanent rejection or claim the current boundary must never change.

Possible follow-up. What would justify a change? Relevant audience evidence, rights clearance and creative approval.

Q12 • Evidence quality

Is Unity proof that AI improves productivity?

Answer route. No. The chart measures reported use, so it establishes plausible candidate applications. The causal productivity support comes from field experiments, not the adoption percentage. The local pilot then determines whether benefits materialize in Square Enix’s own tasks.

Evidence / quote bank: Unity (2026) [S01]; Cui et al. (2026) [S04]
Slide to open: Main 1; B2.

Concede. Unity is a commercial engine provider and the survey is not the entire industry.

Possible follow-up. Why show it? To explain candidate selection, not to compute returns.

Q&A rehearsal cards | 13–15

Q13 • Evidence quality

Are the coding studies directly transferable to games?

Answer route. Not automatically. They establish potential and context sensitivity in software work. The game-testing deployment report provides game-specific feasibility evidence, but uses reinforcement learning rather than the same coding assistant. Transfer must be checked for the engine, workflow and quality demands at hand.

Evidence / quote bank: Cui et al. (2026) [S04]; Becker et al. (2025) [S05]; Gillberg et al. (2023) [S13]
Slide to open: B2; B7.

Concede. Different AI technologies and populations cannot be pooled into one effect.

Possible follow-up. What would you pilot? Narrow approved tasks with independent acceptance tests.

Q14 • Evidence quality

The METR slowdown is old. Why use it?

Answer route. Only as a lesson about measurement and context, not a verdict on present tools. The 2026 update suggests greater benefits may now exist but finds the later estimate unreliable. That reinforces evaluating current tools and rechecking results, rather than relying on either an old negative or positive number.

Evidence / quote bank: Becker et al. (2025) [S05]; Becker et al. (2026) [S06]
Slide to open: Main 4; B2.

Concede. The historical 19% does not predict today’s performance.

Possible follow-up. Why not quote the newer speedup? The authors warn it is unreliable.

Q15 • Evidence quality

Can you compare +26.08% with +19% directly?

Answer route. No. One is completed-task output in pooled company trials; the other is task completion time in a small historical open-source experiment. They appear in separate evidence cards to illustrate context dependence, not on a shared axis, and are not subtracted, averaged or converted into a company forecast.

Evidence / quote bank: Cui et al. (2026) [S04]; Becker et al. (2025) [S05]; Becker et al. (2026) [S06]
Slide to open: B2.

Concede. The measures, populations and tools differ.

Possible follow-up. What uncertainty is disclosed? Cui’s reported standard error; METR’s published interval and update.

Q&A rehearsal cards | 16–18

Q16 • Evidence quality

Is Game8 a solid enough basis for a company-wide rule?

Answer route. It is useful as a direct, game-specific descriptive signal, but insufficient alone for a company-wide rule. We combine it with the client’s creative priorities and authorship research, then identify the final boundary as our judgment. Representative fan work would be a sensible validation task, not a missing sales estimate to invent.

Evidence / quote bank: Dapa (2025) [S07]; Square Enix Holdings Co., Ltd. (2025a) [S02]; Bellaiche et al. (2023) [S08]
Slide to open: B6.

Concede. The sample is small and self-selected; no causal sales conclusion follows.

Possible follow-up. Would your recommendation survive without it? Technical validation remains; the audience-specific creative rationale would be weaker.

Q17 • Pilot and measurement

How would you measure whether a workflow actually helps?

Answer route. Compare similar tasks with and without assistance, randomized where feasible. Track total human effort through review, rework and integration; assess independently accepted output, escaped defects and regressions. Record tool/model versions and task selection. Predefine the success criteria before observing results.

Evidence / quote bank: Cui et al. (2026) [S04]; Becker et al. (2025) [S05]; Tabassi (2023) [S09]; Autio et al. (2024) [S10]
Slide to open: B3.

Concede. This is a proposed study design. Task difficulty, learning and selection can still bias comparisons.

Possible follow-up. Would you measure lines of code? No, not as the primary outcome.

Q18 • Pilot and measurement

What numerical threshold triggers expansion?

Answer route. Do not invent one from public sources. Use the baseline and the client’s existing quality tolerance to predefine a decision: meaningful net value after review and costs, no unacceptable quality deterioration, and responsible sign-off. Expand only when enough comparable observations make the result useful for a decision.

Evidence / quote bank: Tabassi (2023) [S09]; Autio et al. (2024) [S10]
Slide to open: B3.

Concede. No universally correct sample size or percentage saving is established here.

Possible follow-up. How do you prevent moving the goalposts? Agree and record criteria before the pilot.

Q&A rehearsal cards | 19–21

Q19 • Pilot and measurement

Can a human reviewer catch every AI mistake?

Answer route. No. A reviewer is one control, not a guarantee. Keep independent tests, existing release checks and incident monitoring; check generated tests against known failures and test oracles rather than letting a model certify itself. Failures should lead to investigation, rollback or suspension.

Evidence / quote bank: Autio et al. (2024) [S10]; Tabassi (2023) [S09]
Slide to open: B3; B4.

Concede. Residual risk remains with both AI-assisted and conventional development.

Possible follow-up. What is the fallback? Restore the approved conventional workflow.

Q20 • Pilot and measurement

Why not use conventional automation instead of AI?

Answer route. Use the simpler effective option when it meets the need. The pilot should compare against the actual current workflow, including ordinary scripts and test automation. The proposal is not an AI quota; an AI workflow that adds cost or uncertainty without enough value should not replace a working baseline.

Evidence / quote bank: Tabassi (2023) [S09]; Gillberg et al. (2023) [S13]
Slide to open: B3.

Concede. No source here proves AI dominates deterministic tools on every task.

Possible follow-up. What is the decision objective? Accepted quality and net value, not novelty.

Q21 • Pilot and measurement

How much will this save, and what budget does it need?

Answer route. Public evidence does not support a defensible Square Enix savings or budget figure. Use staged funding and record licensing, compute, integration, training, review and maintenance costs. Time released is capacity; it becomes cash saving only when an actual expenditure is avoided. Do not promise a shorter release schedule.

Evidence / quote bank: Tabassi (2023) [S09]; Cui et al. (2026) [S04]
Slide to open: B3; B5.

Concede. Internal costs and deployment details are missing.

Possible follow-up. Why still recommend it? A bounded pilot buys information before larger commitments.

Q&A rehearsal cards | 22–24

Q22 • Policy implementation

Who owns and enforces the policy?

Answer route. Propose executive sponsorship and a cross-functional working group. Creative leads define protected content; engineering and QA validate technical outcomes; legal/security approve relevant tools, data and rights. Each workflow has a named operational owner. Use approvals at tool/use-case level and existing release checks, not a committee for every prompt.

Evidence / quote bank: DORA (2026) [S11]; Tabassi (2023) [S09]; Autio et al. (2024) [S10]
Slide to open: B4.

Concede. This is a proposed allocation, not a claim about current company structure.

Possible follow-up. How do staff know the rules? Searchable approved-use guidance, training and an escalation route.

Q23 • Policy implementation

Will governance slow developers down?

Answer route. It can if designed poorly. Pre-approve repeatable low-risk workflows, provide templates and approved tools, and escalate exceptions. Measure review and compliance time inside the net-value calculation. The policy should remove uncertainty while reserving stronger checks for higher-impact uses.

Evidence / quote bank: DORA (2026) [S11]; Tabassi (2023) [S09]
Slide to open: B4.

Concede. Some necessary controls do add cost; that cost must not be hidden.

Possible follow-up. What if the overhead outweighs the gain? Redesign the workflow or do not scale it.

Q24 • Policy implementation

How do you prevent confidential-code leakage or rights problems?

Answer route. Use approved enterprise arrangements and data classifications, check retention and training-use terms, restrict access, and review output provenance where relevant. Do not send confidential assets to unapproved services. Legal and security approval is a prerequisite, not a benefit assumed because a workflow is internal.

Evidence / quote bank: Autio et al. (2024) [S10]; Tabassi (2023) [S09]
Slide to open: B4.

Concede. An approved vendor does not eliminate risk; terms and implementation need verification.

Possible follow-up. Does human-written final content solve all rights issues? No, inputs and tools still need review.

Q&A rehearsal cards | 25–27

Q25 • Policy implementation

Does internal AI mean you do not disclose anything?

Answer route. No. The recommendation is about appropriate use, not hiding it. Keep internal records and make required platform or stakeholder disclosures. Steam distinguishes efficiency tooling from player-consumed generated content, but that specific platform rule does not replace broader contractual or legal obligations.

Evidence / quote bank: Valve (n.d.) [S14]; Autio et al. (2024) [S10]
Slide to open: B6.

Concede. Requirements can change and differ by platform or jurisdiction.

Possible follow-up. Would you label the game AI-free? Not without a precise, supportable definition.

Q26 • Long-term delivery

Why three to five years, rather than immediately or in one year?

Answer route. The horizon separates immediate testing from integration across teams and durable improvement. It is a planning choice aligned to the scope of organizational change, not a predicted technology timetable. Useful applications can start now; later expansion depends on results and readiness, not simply reaching a calendar date.

Evidence / quote bank: Square Enix Holdings Co., Ltd. (2025a) [S02]; DORA (2026) [S11]; DORA (2025) [S12]
Slide to open: Main 6; B5.

Concede. The evidence supports ongoing capabilities, not these exact dates.

Possible follow-up. What if progress is faster? Advance a ready stage without removing its checks.

Q27 • Long-term delivery

What if the technology changes during the roadmap?

Answer route. Keep the objectives stable but the approved implementations revisable. Re-evaluate after material model, provider, data or task changes. Version the tool and the evaluation. Maintain conventional fallbacks so the company is not locked into a workflow that no longer meets its standards.

Evidence / quote bank: Becker et al. (2026) [S06]; Tabassi (2023) [S09]; DORA (2026) [S11]
Slide to open: B5.

Concede. We do not predict the best model or vendor three years from now.

Possible follow-up. How often? Regular reviews plus event-triggered reassessment; exact cadence is proposed locally.

Q&A rehearsal cards | 28–30

Q28 • Long-term delivery

Does this recommendation imply layoffs?

Answer route. No headcount reduction is part of the proposal. Begin by redirecting released effort toward quality and higher-value work, with training and employee feedback. We cannot guarantee employment outcomes or infer them from an automation target. Workforce effects should be reviewed as an explicit impact.

Evidence / quote bank: Square Enix Holdings Co., Ltd. (2025a) [S02]; Tabassi (2023) [S09]; DORA (2026) [S11]
Slide to open: B4; B5.

Concede. Neither the cited productivity studies nor the target determine staffing decisions.

Possible follow-up. Why retain human skills? The policy depends on informed reviewers and creative ownership.

Q29 • Long-term delivery

What if one studio succeeds but another does not?

Answer route. Do not assume transfer. Share tools, evaluation methods and lessons, then revalidate in the receiving team’s engine, task mix and quality process. Standardize minimum controls, not every technical choice. Stop or redesign where the measured value fails to transfer.

Evidence / quote bank: Gillberg et al. (2023) [S13]; Tabassi (2023) [S09]; DORA (2025) [S12]
Slide to open: B5.

Concede. A single pilot cannot establish company-wide effectiveness.

Possible follow-up. What is shared? Evidence and controls, not an untested promise of identical gains.

Q30 • Policy boundaries

Does copyright law require your creative boundary?

Answer route. Not as a universal rule. The U.S. Copyright Office’s 2025 report distinguishes human-authored expression from purely generated material and allows protection of human contributions in assisted works. Our creative boundary is a business policy; rights questions require jurisdiction- and fact-specific review.

Evidence / quote bank: U.S. Copyright Office (2025) [S15]
Slide to open: B6.

Concede. Do not say AI art is globally illegal or that any AI use destroys copyright.

Possible follow-up. Is legal compliance enough for acceptance? No; creative strategy and audience expectations are separate questions.

Q&A rehearsal cards | 31–32

Q31 • Presentation and logic

You have no regression for AI. Is this recommendation unsupported?

Answer route. No regression in the supplied sales dataset estimates AI’s effect. This recommendation uses relevant external experiments, surveys, company disclosures and risk guidance. We distinguish observed evidence from the proposed policy. The assessment guide allows recommendations grounded in relevant literature rather than a direct model result.

Evidence / quote bank: Unity (2026) [S01]; Cui et al. (2026) [S04]; Tabassi (2023) [S09]
Slide to open: B7.

Concede. Do not imply the group’s IP regression proves an AI benefit; guide p. 8 is the course basis.

Possible follow-up. What is your contribution? Connecting the evidence to a bounded, testable long-term decision.

Q32 • Presentation and logic

What finding would make you change the recommendation?

Answer route. If local trials show no worthwhile net benefit, reduce or stop the technical rollout. If relevant audience, rights and creative evidence supports a different boundary, revise it through the appropriate governance route. Our decision rule is evidence-responsive; a technical productivity gain alone cannot authorize creative replacement.

Evidence / quote bank: Becker et al. (2026) [S06]; Tabassi (2023) [S09]; DORA (2026) [S11]
Slide to open: Main 5–6.

Concede. The proposal is conditional, not a claim that all its choices are already proven optimal.

Possible follow-up. What remains stable? Human accountability, transparent decisions and protection against unacceptable quality or rights risks.

Why the simple policy flow is defensible

DecisionSupporting principleSource locator
ClassifySpecify use and context; approve tool and data.S09: MAP 2.1 / MAP 3; S10: GV-6.1; S11: three-bucket guidance
Creative boundaryProtect important final expression; a strategic choice.S02 p. 7; S07; S08
VerifyBenefits, costs, safety and human oversight.S09 p. 27; S10 p. 32, MS-2.6-004
Scale and reviewMonitor and improve; recover or decommission.S09 p. 33, MANAGE 4; S11

Note. Proposed decision process for Square Enix, informed by Autio et al. (2024), DORA (2026), and Tabassi (2023). The creative boundary and implementation period are consultancy proposals, not prescribed by these sources.

Citation and claim checks

Use author–year citations, not source IDs alone

Paraphrase: (Unity, 2026). Narrative: Cui et al. (2026). Multiple sources: (Autio et al., 2024; Tabassi, 2023). IDs such as S01 only help you navigate this pack.

Direct quotations need locators

Use a printed page for PDFs, e.g. (Tabassi, 2023, p. 27), or the actual section and paragraph where available. Do not invent pages for webpages. Game8’s English gloss is our translation/paraphrase, not an original English quotation.

Separate what the chart depicts

Unity: reported uses, not efficiency gains; selected technical categories, not an exhaustive ranking. Game8: approximate positive responses, not all-player purchase intent. Productivity cards: incompatible outcomes shown separately, never pooled.

Keep the reference version consistent

The two Square Enix 2025 works are 2025a (Annual report) and 2025b (Progress report). Reconcile these letters with the whole group’s final reference list. The Cui citation follows the verified advance-online publisher record. Valve has no dated publication year and uses n.d. with a retrieval date.

Reference formatting

The full list below is alphabetical with italicized titles, double spacing and 0.5-inch hanging indents. Clipboard rich text preserves formatting when supported; check formatting after pasting into Word or PowerPoint.

Avoid these claims: 70% cost savings; all players reject AI artwork; 48% positive means 52% opposed; human approval guarantees correctness; a coding result predicts game sales; NIST proves a 3–5-year optimum; public sources show Square Enix has no governance.
